newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti PC talks well advanced -- unions.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti PC talks well advanced -- unions.

text.p: Talks are well advanced over the sale of Olivetti's loss-making personal computer company, which the Italian information technology group is aiming to sell by the end of this year, union sources said on Wednesday.

Trade union leaders met with Industry Minister Pier Luigi Bersani late Tuesday, and union sources said that talks were on course to see a sale of the PC company by end-1996, a timetable set by Olivetti's chief executive Roberto Colaninno.

The union sources said Colaninno had said the deal to sell part of Olivetti's stake in mobile phone consortium Omnitel to German group Mannesmann had put a value of 2.7 trillion lire on Olivetti's stake in Omnitel, amounting to just over 35 percent after the Mannesmann deal.
Colaninno said this amount of 2.7 trillion lire was greater than Olivetti's net debts, the union sources said. Olivetti said its net debt was 2.415 trillion lire at end-September.
